8.6 — Boss Studio + Final Review

Your boss works (8.5), and the semester's final is a normal B day — a normal B day where you ship the game you have been building since September. Today is split in two: polish in the studio, then the review that makes sure you can talk about every decision you made, out loud, without notes.

Studio Brief ~30 min

Grade yourself against your own spec first. Open BOSS_SPEC.md from 8.1 and read it line by line next to the running game. Every attack has a telegraph the player can see? Every phase change is visible within a second? The arena is the shape you drew? Write the gaps down before you fix any of them — a spec you never check against the build is a wish, not a specification.

Then the three universal upgrades. Each one is optional, and each one has a real cost in a project this size:

  • Sound. A hit sound on the swing connecting, a wind-up sound under the telegraph, a sound when the boss dies. Audio is half of "feel" and none of "mechanics" — and it would be the first audio in this project, so budget for learning AudioSource from scratch rather than assuming it is one line.
  • Hit feedback. The boss flashes on taking a hit, and the camera nudges on the charge. Be careful with the second one: your camera is driven by a finished script in Assets/Scripts/Package Scripts/, so a shake has to work with somebody else's follow logic rather than around it.
  • The clear screen. When the boss dies, something on screen says so. You own the whole mechanism already: 5.3 put a Canvas, a Text (TMP) and a one-slot script into Start. The hard part is not the UI system — it is that your HUD reads the player's stats and knows nothing about a boss, and it is not in the scene the boss dies in. So this is either one honest printed line, or the day you decide a second HUD is worth solving that scene problem again. TextMesh Pro is already installed, which removes one obstacle and not the other four.

Ship-freeze rules for the review: no new attacks, no new systems, no "just one more mechanic." New things break old things, and the build you demo has to be the most boring build you have made all year.

One honest inventory before you polish anything. This project contains exactly one Coin instance in the entire game. There is no coin economy, no shop, and nothing that spends a coin. That is not a failure — it is the truth about what you built, and the review will go better if you can say it before anyone else does. Decide now: do you place more coins and give them a purpose, or do you leave the single coin and describe it accurately as a demonstration of the pickup system? Both are defensible. "I did not notice" is not.

Socratic: What Did You Actually Ship?

  1. Name the one thing in your game that a stranger would remember after playing it. Is it the boss, the cave, or something you built in an earlier unit?
  2. Your project ships one Coin. Where is it, what does collecting it prove, and what is the honest one-sentence description of your game's economy?
  3. Which system in your game is the most fragile — the one most likely to break if you touched it? What does leaving it alone cost you?
Final Review ~20 min

The final is a normal B day: your game, open, playable, and a conversation about it. Practise that conversation — answer each of these in about thirty seconds, out loud, without looking anything up.

  1. Trace collecting a coin from the moment of contact to the number appearing in the Console. Name every method it passes through — and say which object the number now lives on, and why it moved there (2.1, 5.3).
  2. Draw your boss's state machine from memory, with the transition condition written on every arrow (4.5, 8.4).
  3. Explain Time.deltaTime to someone who has never written code (1.5).
  4. Why is your jump "tight"? Name the three values you tuned (6.3).
  5. Where did you use the cooldown pattern? Count every instance in your game — the turret, then the enemy or the hazard, then your swing, then any attack the boss telegraphs.
  6. Where does the boss's health live, and where does the player's? Explain the difference in one sentence using the word lifetime (8.2).
  7. What does Physics2D.queriesHitTriggers default to, and what did you do about it in your ground check (8.3)?
  8. If you built a UnityEvent on your boss's death, what does it decouple? If you did not, say what you did instead and what it cost you (5.2, 8.5).
  9. Which beat of your cave killed the most playtesters, and what is the data behind that claim (7.7)?

Socratic: Inherit, Extend, Create

  1. Your game is a program built by forking a starter. What did you inherit unchanged, what did you extend by turning its knobs, and what did you create from nothing?
  2. Which of the three categories is the largest in your project — and is that the answer you expected in September?
  3. The boss, the arena and the boss door were not in the starter; you built all three. Where is the line between "using a library" and "authorship" — and which side of it does your boss fall on?

Checkpoint — the semester, complete:

  • One full run, from first control to the fight resolving, played and bug-listed
  • Spec graded line by line; every remaining gap has a reason, not an excuse
  • All nine review answers said out loud, without notes
  • The single-coin fact known and described accurately, not discovered by someone else
  • Repo tagged and pushed — the playable build is the portfolio
